mainTopic: Farm work on חול המועד and in שביעית: כלאים, watering fields, and dealing with pests
overview: The amud opens with the last line of a ruling about seed mixtures, then asks why the משנה has agents uproot כלאים when a ברייתא says the whole field is declared הפקר. The answer is that the two sources describe different times, and a ברייתא tells how the תקנה grew stricter in three stages. A new משנה brings a מחלוקת about watering on חול המועד. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב allows leading water from tree to tree but not watering a whole field, and חכמים are more lenient. רב יהודה and a ברייתא say that a field that was moist before the מועד may be watered. רבינא learns from this that a garden may be sprinkled, because watering makes a late crop come early. Two ברייתות about sprinkling a שדה לבן seem to clash, and רב הונא assigns each to a different side of the מחלוקת. Another משנה allows trapping moles and mice, patching a broken wall on the מועד, and building it normally in שביעית. The גמרא explains what an אישות is and how to destroy ant nests.

steps.title: A seed mixture with a quarter of another kind must be reduced
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of a ruling about seed mixtures: a quarter-measure of a different species of seed requires the owner to reduce it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a quarter-measure of seed from a different species mixed in, the owner must reduce it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ruling about seed mixtures. If enough seed of another kind is mixed in, the owner has to thin it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line sets a minimum amount. Below it, the mixed-in seed is not a problem. At this amount, the owner must actively remove some of the other species so the field does not become כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter (here, a quarter of a קַב measure)

phrases.english: A quarter of seed from a different species: he must reduce it.
phrases.notes: Literally just 'a quarter.' It means a quarter-קַב, the measure given earlier in this ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a source the גמרא was quoting just before this section, about the laws of כלאים in seed mixtures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A quarter-measure of another species mixed into seed must be reduced.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the whole field is declared ownerless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that agents uproot כלאים. A ברייתא says חכמים ruled to declare the entire field הפקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: they made a rule that the entire field should be declared ownerless!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. The משנה says agents go out and uproot כלאים, but a ברייתא says the whole field is made ownerless instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Uprooting only removes the bad plants. Declaring the field הפקר takes away the owner's whole crop. These are two very different responses, so the גמרא asks which one is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But it was taught: they instituted that they should declare ownerless
the entire field, all of it!
phrases.notes: This means a field where כלאים was found. Anyone may then take its crop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the משנה's rule about going out to deal with כלאים and challenges it from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that agents of בית דין go out and uproot כלאים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא records a different procedure, declaring the whole field הפקר, which seems to contradict uprooting.

steps.title: Before the new rule and after it
steps.stepSummary: No contradiction: the משנה describes the time before the תקנה, and the ברייתא describes the time after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it is before the תקנה; there, it is after the תקנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by placing the two sources in different time periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources are correct, each for its own era. Uprooting was the original practice. Later חכמים made a stricter תקנה to declare the field הפקר.

keyTerms.meaning: Here ... there (each source refers to a different case)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not rejecting the משנה. It describes a later stage, after חכמים changed the practice.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it is before the enactment;
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the משנה, which talks about uprooting.

phrases.english: there, it is after the enactment.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן קוֹדֶם תַּקָּנָה כָּאן לְאַחַר תַּקָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time period (before and after a תקנה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא describe the same situation with conflicting rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה reflects the original practice, and the ברייתא reflects the later תקנה.

steps.title: Stage one: uprooting and feeding the animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the answer. At first, agents uprooted the כלאים and threw them to the owners' animals, which made the owners happy for two reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: At first they would uproot the כלאים and throw them before the owners' animals. The owners were happy twice over: once because their fields got weeded, and once because their animals got fed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the תקנה really did change over time. It begins with the original practice and its problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first practice backfired. The owners got free weeding and free animal feed, so they had no reason to keep כלאים out of their fields. This sets up the need for a stricter rule.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (introduces a supporting ברייתא)

phrases.english: As it was taught: At first,
they would uproot and throw them before their animals.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the agents of בית דין, and 'their animals' belong to the field owners.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ בַּעֲלֵי בָּתִּים שְׂמֵחִין שְׁתֵּי שְׂמָחוֹת:
phrases.english: And the property owners would rejoice with two joys:
one, that their fields were weeded for them,
and one, that they threw them before their animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source showing there really was a 'before' and 'after' the תקנה.
steps.raayaObject: The answer in step 3 that the practice changed over time.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recounting the history of the תקנה.

steps.title: Stages two and three: throwing on the roads, then הפקר
steps.stepSummary: חכמים ruled to throw the uprooted plants on the roads. Owners were still glad about the free weeding, so חכמים finally ruled to declare the whole field הפקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They instituted that the plants be uprooted and thrown on the roads. Still, the owners rejoiced greatly that their fields were weeded. So they instituted that the entire field be declared ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the story. It ends with the exact rule that the ברייתא in step 2 quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each step closed one benefit. Throwing on the roads removed the free animal feed, but the free weeding remained. Declaring the field הפקר removed every benefit, so it now cost the owner to leave כלאים in his field.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule of declaring the field הפקר was the final stage of a three-step תקנה. Each stage was meant to stop owners from benefiting when כלאים grew in their fields. The משנה's 'uprooting' reflects the earlier stage.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that חכמים adjusted their rules when people found a benefit in them, to make sure the rule actually discouraged the problem.

phrases.english: They instituted that they should uproot
and throw them on the roads.
And still they would rejoice with great joy
that their fields were weeded.
So they instituted that they should declare ownerless
the entire field, all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ עוֹקְרִין וּמַשְׁלִיכִין עַל הַדְּרָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא through its last two stages.
steps.raayaObject: That declaring the field הפקר came after the earlier practice of uprooting.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rest of the ברייתא, which ends with the words of the ברייתא from step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה (uprooting) and the ברייתא (הפקר) reflect different stages of one developing תקנה.

steps.title: The new משנה: limits on watering during the festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב allows leading water from tree to tree, but not watering the whole field. He also forbids watering plants that were not watered before the מועד. חכמים permit both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: on חול המועד a person may lead water from one tree to the next, as long as he does not water the entire field. Plants that were not watered before the מועד may not be watered during the מועד. חכמים permit watering in both of these cases.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a מחלוקת about how much watering is allowed on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב sets two limits. Trees may get water, but the whole field may not. Plants that were never watered before the מועד may not be watered now. חכמים disagree and allow both.

keyTerms.meaning: Leading or drawing water along through channels
The festival; here it means חול המועד, the in-between days
In this case and in that case, meaning both cases

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
One may draw the water from tree to tree,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַשְׁקֶה אֶת כׇּל הַשָּׂדֶה.
phrases.english: provided that he does not water the entire field.
Plants that did not drink before the Festival —
he may not water them on the Festival.
But the Sages permit in this and in that.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the earlier discussion about כלאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, water may be led from tree to tree but the whole field may not be watered, and unwatered plants may not be watered on the מועד. חכמים permit both.

steps.title: רב יהודה: a field that was moist may be watered
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that if the field was moist before the מועד, watering it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: if the field had been moist, it is permitted to water it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב יהודה, who adds an exception to the limits in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A field that was already moist before the מועד is treated like a field that was watered. So even רבי אליעזר בן יעקב would allow watering it during the מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא, marking where the גמרא starts
A moist field, one that already had moisture before the מועד

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a third opinion. רב יהודה is explaining that the limit of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב does not apply to a field that was moist.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yehuda said:
If the field was moist — it is permitted.
phrases.notes: He means moist before the מועד. It then dried out, and now it needs water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: אִם הָיְתָה שָׂדֶה מְטוּנֶּנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A field that was moist before the מועד may be watered during the מועד.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב יהודה and spells out the full rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the ban applies only to plants that were never watered before the מועד. A moist field is permitted. A dry field may not be watered, but חכמים permit both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: when they said it is forbidden to water on the מועד, they meant only plants that were not watered before the מועד. Plants that were watered before the מועד may be watered during it. If the field was moist, it is permitted. A dry field may not be watered on the מועד. חכמים permit both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says just what רב יהודה said, which supports his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that the ban is narrow: only plants that never got water before the מועד are forbidden. Plants already watered, and a field that was already moist, may be watered. It also names the forbidden case, a שדה גריד, and records that חכמים permit even that.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way, introducing a ברייתא that supports the statement just made
They said it only about, which narrows a rule
A dry field that has no moisture at all

steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא sets out exactly where the ban applies. רבינא's lesson in the next step builds on the fact that חכמים permit watering a שדה גריד.

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
When they said it is forbidden to water them on the Festival,
they said it only about plants
that did not drink from before the Festival,
but plants that drank before the Festival —
it is permitted to water them on the Festival.
And if the field was moist — it is permitted.
And one may not water a dry field on the Festival,
and the Sages permit in this and in that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רב יהודה's exception with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that a שדה מטוננת may be watered.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says outright that a moist field may be watered.

steps.title: רבינא: a person may sprinkle a garden on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רבינא learns from the ברייתא that sprinkling a small garden is permitted on חול המועד. Watering a dry field is allowed because it makes a late crop come early, and sprinkling a garden does the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: learn from this that it is permitted to sprinkle a garden on חול המועד. Why may a dry field be watered? Because watering turns a late crop into an early one. Here too, sprinkling turns a late crop into an early one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא draws a new practical lesson from the ruling of חכמים about a dry field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plants in a dry field will not die without water, yet חכמים permit watering it. The reason must be that watering makes the crop ripen early, and losing that early crop counts as a real loss. Sprinkling a garden also makes its crop come early, so it is permitted too.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, introducing a conclusion drawn from a source
The weekdays of the festival, meaning חול המועד

steps.whatToRemember: On חול המועד, watering is permitted not only to keep plants from dying. It is also permitted to make a late crop come early, and this is why חכמים allow watering a dry field and sprinkling a garden.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Learn from this
that this garden — it is permitted to sprinkle it
on the intermediate days of the Festival.
A dry field — what is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking why חכמים let you water a dry field, since its plants would not die without water.

phrases.english: Because it turns a late crop into an early one,
here too,
it turns a late crop into an early one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ruling of חכמים in the ברייתא about a dry field and applies its reason to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sprinkling a garden on חול המועד is permitted, because it makes a late crop into an early one.

steps.title: A ברייתא: sprinkling is allowed in שביעית but not on the מועד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may sprinkle water on a שדה לבן in שביעית, but not on the מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may sprinkle water on a grain field during the seventh year, but not during חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about sprinkling water on an open grain field. It allows this in שביעית but forbids it on the מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא treats the מועד more strictly than שביעית for this action. On the מועד, sprinkling the field is not allowed at all. This sets up the contradiction the גמרא will raise next.

keyTerms.meaning: We sprinkle water lightly on the ground
An open field of grain or vegetables, with no trees
The seventh year, when working the land is limited
The Rabbis taught; this opens a ברייתא

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may sprinkle a white field during the seventh year,
phrases.notes: A "white field" is an open field with no trees, usually grain, so no tree shade covers it.

phrases.english: but not on the מועד.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַרְבִּיצִין שְׂדֵה לָבָן בַּשְּׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of watering fields on the מועד with a new ברייתא that also mentions שביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sprinkling a שדה לבן is allowed in שביעית but forbidden on the מועד.

steps.title: A different ברייתא allows sprinkling on the מועד too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא with another ברייתא that allows sprinkling both on the מועד and in שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in another ברייתא: One may sprinkle both on the מועד and in the seventh year!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that another ברייתא says the opposite. That one allows sprinkling on the מועד too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות disagree about the מועד only. The first forbids sprinkling on the מועד, and the second allows it. Both agree it is fine in שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught? This introduces a contradicting ברייתא

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
One may sprinkle both on the מועד and during the seventh year!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 10 with a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's ban on sprinkling on the מועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give opposite rulings for the same case on the מועד, so one of them seems wrong.

steps.title: רב הונא: each ברייתא follows a different opinion
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the strict ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the lenient one follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and that one follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא settles the contradiction. Each ברייתא matches one side of a מחלוקת we already learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב forbade watering a whole field on the מועד, and the חכמים permitted it. So the ברייתא that forbids sprinkling follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and the one that allows it follows the רבנן. The two ברייתות are not in conflict; they record two different opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
This one... that one... It splits the two sources between two views

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on sprinkling a field on the מועד is only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view. The רבנן allow it.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: It is not difficult:
This one is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא, the one that forbids sprinkling on the מועד. It fits his view from step 6, where he forbids watering a whole field.

phrases.english: that one is the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different opinion in a known מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to contradict each other about the מועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the lenient one follows the רבנן, as in step 6.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: sprinkling before and during שביעית
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא allows sprinkling a שדה לבן on ערב שביעית so vegetables come up in שביעית, and even in שביעית so they come up after it ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: One may sprinkle a grain field on the eve of the seventh year so that vegetables will come up in the seventh year. And more than that, one may sprinkle a grain field during the seventh year so that vegetables will come up after the seventh year ends.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא about sprinkling in connection with שביעית. It shows how far the permission to sprinkle goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first allows sprinkling before שביעית, even though the plants will grow during שביעית. Then it adds that sprinkling is allowed even during שביעית itself, as long as the vegetables come up only after שביעית ends. This shows that sprinkling is treated as a light action.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but even... It adds a bigger point
The time right after שביעית ends

phrases.english: Another ברייתא teaches:
One may sprinkle a white field on the eve of the seventh year
so that vegetables will come up during the seventh year,
and not only that, but
one may sprinkle a white field during the seventh year
so that vegetables will come up after the seventh year ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ברייתא about how far sprinkling is allowed in שביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sprinkling a שדה לבן is allowed on ערב שביעית for growth in שביעית, and even in שביעית for growth after it ends.

steps.title: New משנה: trapping moles and mice in fields
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says one may trap moles and mice in an orchard and a grain field in the usual way on the מועד and in שביעית. The חכמים allow the usual way only in an orchard, and in a grain field only in an unusual way.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may trap moles and mice from an orchard and from a grain field in the usual way, on the מועד and in the seventh year. But the חכמים say: From an orchard, in the usual way; from a grain field, only in an unusual way.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with catching pests that damage fields, on the מועד and in שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion allows normal trapping in both kinds of field. The חכמים make a difference: in an orchard normal trapping is fine, but in a grain field one must trap in an unusual way. So the מחלוקת is only about the grain field.

keyTerms.meaning: A mole, an animal that digs under the ground
An orchard, a field of trees

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים do not forbid trapping in a grain field. They only require it to be done in an unusual way.

phrases.english: משנה:
One may trap moles and mice
from an orchard and from a white field
in the usual way, on the מועד and in the seventh year.
And the Sages say:
From an orchard, in the usual way,
and from a white field, not in the usual way.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ צָדִין אֶת הָאִישׁוּת וְאֶת הָעַכְבָּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: trapping pests instead of watering fields.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion allows trapping in the usual way in both kinds of field. The חכמים require an unusual way in a שדה לבן.

steps.title: Patching a broken wall on the מועד, building in שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends: on the מועד one may only patch a gap in a wall, but in שביעית one may build it the normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may patch up a breach in a wall on the מועד, and in שביעית one may build it in the usual way.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It allows a simple patch of a broken wall on the מועד, and full normal building in שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two times have different limits. On the מועד only a quick, partial fix is allowed. In שביעית, building a wall is not farm work, so one may build it fully and normally.

keyTerms.meaning: patch up, cover over (a quick fix)
a breach or gap in a wall

phrases.english: And one may patch up the breach on the מועד,
and in שביעית one builds in his usual way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה begun in step 14, adding a new ruling about walls.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מועד: only patching a breach is allowed. שביעית: one may build normally.

steps.title: What is an אישות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the word אישות in the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is an אישות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה by asking what kind of creature an אישות is. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 14) allowed trapping an אישות but never said what it is. Before the rule can be applied, we need to know which animal is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
a burrowing creature that harms fields (a mole)

phrases.english: גמרא: What is an אישות?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by clarifying a word from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the creature called אישות.

steps.title: רב יהודה: a creature with no eyes
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that an אישות is a creature that has no eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is a creature that has no eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question: the אישות is an eyeless creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He identifies it by a clear feature, being blind. This fits a mole, an animal that lives underground and digs through fields.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A creature that has no eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אישות is an eyeless creature.

steps.title: A פסוק showing the אישות never sees the sun
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר ישמעאל (or רב יימר בר שלמיא) brings a פסוק in תהלים that describes an אשת that never sees the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר ישמעאל said, and some say it was רב יימר בר שלמיא: What is the פסוק for this? 'Like a snail that melts away as it goes; like the fall of an אשת that has not seen the sun.'
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא brings a פסוק to support רב יהודה's answer. The פסוק speaks of an אשת that has never seen the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אשת in the פסוק is read as the same creature as the אישות. It never sees the sun because it has no eyes, which matches רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the פסוק (that shows this)?
and some say (it was someone else who said it)

phrases.english: Rava bar Yishmael said,
and some say it was Rav Yeimar bar Shelamya:
What is the verse?
"Like a snail that melts away as it goes,
like the fall of an eshet that has not seen the sun."
phrases.notes: The אשת here is the אישות. It never sees the sun because it has no eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's answer with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the אישות is an eyeless creature.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 58:9: an אשת that never saw the sun.

steps.title: ברייתא: trapping moles and mice, and destroying ant holes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows trapping moles and mice normally in both fields, and adds that one may destroy ant holes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may trap moles and mice from a grain field and from an orchard in the usual way, and one may destroy ant holes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that repeats the trapping rule. It then adds something new: destroying ant holes is also allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the first opinion in the משנה, this ברייתא allows normal trapping in both kinds of fields. Its new point is that ants can also be dealt with, since they too damage the field.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may trap moles and mice
from a grain field and from an orchard in the usual way,
and one may destroy ant holes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the אישות to a ברייתא that adds to the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trapping in both fields in the normal way is allowed, and ant holes may be destroyed.

steps.title: How are ant holes destroyed?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how one goes about destroying ant holes.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one destroy them?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how exactly one gets rid of the ant holes. This sets up רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allowed destroying ant holes but did not say how. The question asks for the method.

phrases.english: How does one destroy them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the method behind the ruling in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The method of destroying ant holes.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: mix soil between nests
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says to move soil from one ant hole into another, so the ants strangle each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: One brings soil from this hole and puts it into that hole, and they strangle each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explains the method: mix soil from one nest into another, and the ants kill each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ants from two different nests do not know each other. Putting them together makes them fight and kill each other, so the field is cleared.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One brings soil from this hole
and puts it into that hole,
and they strangle each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Move soil from one ant hole into another so the two groups of ants kill each other.

steps.title: אביי: the trick works only when the nests are fully separated
steps.stepSummary: Quoting אביי, רב יימר בר שלמיא limits the method to nests on two sides of a river with no bridge, plank or rope between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר בר שלמיא said in the name of אביי: This works only when the nests are on two sides of a river, when there is no bridge, when there is no plank, and when there is no rope.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds conditions to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's method. It only works if the two nests are on opposite sides of a river with nothing at all connecting them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trick depends on the ants being total strangers. If there is any way across, even a plank or a rope, the ants may already know each other and will not fight. So the soil must come from a fully cut-off nest.
steps.whatToRemember: Moles, mice and ants all damage fields, so the רבנן allow dealing with them. The ant method of mixing soil only works when the two nests have no connection at all.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar bar Shelamya said in the name of Abaye:
And this is only when they are on two sides of a river,
and only when there is no bridge,
and only when there is no plank,
and only when there is no rope.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's method to a specific situation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The soil trick works only when the nests are on opposite sides of a river with no bridge, plank or rope connecting them.
